item.title: Two killed in head-on collision on Baldwin Beach Express near Robertsdale
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Two people died in a head-on crash on the Baldwin Beach Express near Robertsdale, Alabama, on Sunday evening, according to the Robertsdale Police Department. The collision occurred around 7 p.m. on the heavily-traveled route that connects the Gulf Shores area to inland communities. Robertsdale police are continuing to investigate the circumstances…
item.content:encoded: Two people died in a head-on crash on the Baldwin Beach Express near Robertsdale, Alabama, on Sunday evening, according to the Robertsdale Police Department. The collision occurred around 7 p.m. on the heavily-traveled route that connects the Gulf Shores area to inland communities. Robertsdale police are continuing to investigate the circumstances of the crash. The Baldwin Beach Express, also known as Alabama Highway 231, is a major corridor during peak travel times, particularly on weekends when beachgoers head to and from the coast. No additional details about the victims or what led to the head-on impact were immediately available. The incident marks another serious traffic fatality in the region, which sees significant seasonal traffic increases.

item.content:encoded:
YouTube personality Jack Doherty was arrested Friday in Fort Lauderdale on a misdemeanor domestic battery charge following a physical dispute at a residence in the Riverside Park neighborhood.

Fort Lauderdale police responded to the home just before noon Friday, where officers found Doherty and a woman involved in a physical altercation inside the residence. According to investigators, the woman was not injured in the incident.

The 22-year-old was taken into custody and booked into the Broward County Jail. He faces a misdemeanor domestic battery charge stemming from the incident.

item.title: Florida July Revenue Misses Forecast, But State Revises Outlook Upward
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Florida's general revenue collections for July fell slightly short of state projections, coming in at $3.68 billion—about $16 million below what economists predicted in January. The shortfall was driven primarily by underperformance in real estate documentary stamp taxes and beverage taxes. However, the state found some bright spots in the report:…
item.content:encoded:
Florida's general revenue collections for July fell slightly short of state projections, coming in at $3.68 billion—about $16 million below what economists predicted in January.

The shortfall was driven primarily by underperformance in real estate documentary stamp taxes and beverage taxes. However, the state found some bright spots in the report: sales tax and corporate income tax both outperformed their forecasts, suggesting underlying economic strength in consumer spending and business activity.

Despite the July miss, state economists responded with optimism about Florida's fiscal trajectory. They've revised revenue projections upward by nearly $1 billion beginning with August's report, signaling confidence that the state's economy is performing better than initially anticipated when the year began.

The mixed results highlight the volatility in Florida's revenue streams, particularly in property-related taxes that depend on real estate market conditions. The upward revision for coming months suggests economists believe recent economic momentum will continue through the remainder of the fiscal year.

item.title: Florida Board of Governors seeks new rules for college athlete compensation
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Florida's Board of Governors is asking state legislators and Congress to step up regulation of college sports, particularly around athlete compensation and agent oversight. A task force chaired by Governor Ken Jones wants the NCAA granted antitrust exemption status to establish a salary cap and set eligibility rules—moves that would fundamentally…
item.content:encoded:
Florida's Board of Governors is asking state legislators and Congress to step up regulation of college sports, particularly around athlete compensation and agent oversight. A task force chaired by Governor Ken Jones wants the NCAA granted antitrust exemption status to establish a salary cap and set eligibility rules—moves that would fundamentally reshape how student-athletes are paid and managed.

The recommendations also include a "commercially reasonable" registration fee for athletic agents, financial literacy training requirements for student-athletes, and trust structures to help young athletes manage their earnings. The push reflects growing concern that current rules don't adequately protect student-athletes from predatory practices or prepare them to handle sudden wealth.

The timing matters: Congress is actively debating the Protect College Sports Act, with Senate debate expected to begin later this month. That federal legislation could override state rules and NCAA policies, making this the moment Florida's higher education leadership is making its voice heard. The Board of Governors' recommendations aim to influence what that final law might look like—and whether states or federal agencies get the final say on how college athletes are compensated and represented.

item.title: BJ's Employee Charged in $18K Theft Scheme Using Fake Scanning
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A 71-year-old Boynton Beach BJ's Wholesale Club employee has been arrested after police say he helped customers steal nearly $18,000 in merchandise over several months. Angel Camacho-Flores worked at the store's exit, where investigators say he would fake-scan items to make fraudulent purchases appear legitimate. The scheme allowed customers to…
item.content:encoded:
A 71-year-old Boynton Beach BJ's Wholesale Club employee has been arrested after police say he helped customers steal nearly $18,000 in merchandise over several months.

Angel Camacho-Flores worked at the store's exit, where investigators say he would fake-scan items to make fraudulent purchases appear legitimate. The scheme allowed customers to walk out with unpaid merchandise while the transactions looked legal on the register.

Police say Camacho-Flores admitted his role in the theft ring. Rather than receiving cash payments, he told authorities he was compensated with groceries and gift cards from the store. Investigators did not disclose how many customers may have been involved or over what specific time period the thefts occurred.

The case remains under investigation. Camacho-Flores is facing theft charges related to the scheme.

item.title: Tampa Man Charged After Breaking Into Elderly Woman's Apartment
item.dc:creator: newsroom

Deputies say the woman initially believed the man, identified as Connor Norcross, was her grandson before realizing he was a stranger. She told him to…
item.content:encoded:
A 24-year-old Tampa man is facing burglary and elder battery charges after allegedly breaking into a 93-year-old woman's apartment and standing at the foot of her bed, according to investigators.

Deputies say the woman initially believed the man, identified as Connor Norcross, was her grandson before realizing he was a stranger. She told him to leave the apartment. Before exiting, investigators say Norcross touched her arm. He then attempted to re-enter through the locked front door but was unable to get back inside.

Authorities identified Norcross through security footage from the apartment building. He was arrested days after the incident. The case highlights ongoing concerns about residential security and the vulnerability of elderly residents to home invasions.

item.title: Five Dead in Prime Air Cargo Plane Crash at Miami International Airport
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A Prime Air cargo plane crashed at Miami International Airport on Sunday afternoon, killing five people and injuring five others. The aircraft, Flight 7598, overran a diagonal runway around 2 p.m. and became disabled at the northwest end of the airport, striking multiple vehicles before catching fire. Miami-Dade County officials responded with…
item.content:encoded:
A Prime Air cargo plane crashed at Miami International Airport on Sunday afternoon, killing five people and injuring five others. The aircraft, Flight 7598, overran a diagonal runway around 2 p.m. and became disabled at the northwest end of the airport, striking multiple vehicles before catching fire.

Miami-Dade County officials responded with more than 60 fire-rescue units to the scene. The airport implemented a full ground stop, closing all runways and taxiways while emergency crews worked to contain the situation and investigate the crash.

The incident caused significant disruptions to airport operations. Travelers heading to Miami International Airport are advised to contact their airlines for flight status updates before departing for the airport, as operations have been severely impacted by the closure and ongoing emergency response.

item.title: Florida Universities to Ban Undocumented Students Starting 2027-28
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Florida's Board of Governors voted unanimously Wednesday to prohibit undocumented immigrants from enrolling at the state's 12 public universities, effective with the 2027-2028 academic year. Lieutenant Governor Jay Collins defended the decision, arguing that state taxpayers should not fund educational opportunities for students in the country…
item.content:encoded:
Florida's Board of Governors voted unanimously Wednesday to prohibit undocumented immigrants from enrolling at the state's 12 public universities, effective with the 2027-2028 academic year.

Lieutenant Governor Jay Collins defended the decision, arguing that state taxpayers should not fund educational opportunities for students in the country illegally. "This is common sense policy," Collins said, noting the move aligns Florida's university system with restrictions already in place for public colleges and technical education programs across the state.

The policy applies to all students who lack legal authorization to reside in the United States. Students already enrolled will be permitted to finish their degrees under grandfather provisions, but new admissions will be restricted beginning in fall 2027.

The decision reflects Florida's broader push to limit public benefits and services for undocumented immigrants. The state's community college and technical school systems implemented similar restrictions in recent years. University officials did not immediately detail how the policy would be enforced or what documentation students would need to provide to verify their immigration status.

Education advocates have raised concerns about the potential impact on Florida's workforce development and the state's competitiveness in attracting talent, though the Board of Governors proceeded without dissenting votes.

item.content:encoded:
Kyle Rittenhouse has landed a new job at Shark Coast Tactical in Sarasota, the store announced during a recent podcast episode. Rittenhouse and his wife relocated to the Sarasota area after he accepted the position.

He previously worked at Gulf Coast Gun and Outdoors in Milton, which closed last year. The move represents his first public employment since his high-profile trial in Wisconsin.

Rittenhouse became a nationally recognized figure after a jury acquitted him in 2020 of charges stemming from the Kenosha shootings, determining he acted in self-defense during a confrontation that left two people dead and one wounded.

item.title: Escambia County Corrections adds 9 new officers from academy
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Nine new Corrections Officers have graduated from George Stone Criminal Justice Training Center's Corrections Academy and are joining the Escambia County Department of Corrections. The graduates completed a rigorous 445-hour training program that included defensive tactics, firearms training, and CPR certification. The comprehensive curriculum…
item.content:encoded:
Nine new Corrections Officers have graduated from George Stone Criminal Justice Training Center's Corrections Academy and are joining the Escambia County Department of Corrections.

The graduates completed a rigorous 445-hour training program that included defensive tactics, firearms training, and CPR certification. The comprehensive curriculum prepares officers for the challenges they'll face in the county's correctional facilities.

"We're proud of this new class, and we're excited to watch them grow in their careers," said Commander Scott Nash. The department is working to build up its workforce during a period when correctional staffing has become increasingly competitive nationally.

To attract qualified candidates, Escambia County is offering sign-on bonuses up to $8,000 for certified officers and $5,000 for trainees. The department also provides a paid scholarship to cover academy tuition for recruits who don't already hold certification. These incentives reflect the county's commitment to recruiting and retaining quality personnel in corrections roles.

Kent Blacklidge was placed on administrative leave once the investigation began. The charges represent some…
item.content:encoded:
A 43-year-old Baldwin County man employed as a Homeland Security Investigations special agent has turned himself in on multiple severe sex crime charges, including rape, sodomy, and incest, according to the Escambia County Sheriff's Office.

Kent Blacklidge was placed on administrative leave once the investigation began. The charges represent some of the most serious crimes in the criminal code, and the case has prompted law enforcement to emphasize that investigations proceed regardless of a suspect's employment or status.

"Our job is to pursue justice," Chief John Barber said in a statement regarding the investigation. "That applies to everyone, no matter who they are or where they work."

The Escambia County Sheriff's Office has scheduled a press conference for Tuesday to provide additional details on the case, charges, and investigation. Specific times and location information will be released as the date approaches. Blacklidge remains in custody pending further court proceedings.

Michael Earl Beasley is wanted on attempted homicide and burglary charges stemming from the incident. According to deputies, Beasley stabbed the victim approximately five times during an argument…
item.content:encoded:
A 42-year-old Pensacola man has been arrested in connection with an August stabbing at the Lyons Motel, the Escambia County Sheriff's Office reports.

Michael Earl Beasley is wanted on attempted homicide and burglary charges stemming from the incident. According to deputies, Beasley stabbed the victim approximately five times during an argument before stealing money and fleeing the scene.

The victim was hospitalized for injuries sustained in the attack. Despite an immediate search and perimeter setup by deputies, Beasley initially evaded capture. He was located and arrested Saturday.

The arrest closes an active investigation that had lasted several months since the August incident.

item.title: Escambia County to Vote on $100K State Grant for Beach Cleanup
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Escambia County commissioners will vote Thursday on accepting a $100,000 state grant aimed at tackling sargassum, red tide, and other biological debris washing up on local beaches and waterfronts. The funding marks the first year the state legislature has made this type of money available to counties dealing with marine debris problems. This…
item.content:encoded:
Escambia County commissioners will vote Thursday on accepting a $100,000 state grant aimed at tackling sargassum, red tide, and other biological debris washing up on local beaches and waterfronts. The funding marks the first year the state legislature has made this type of money available to counties dealing with marine debris problems.

This year's sargassum bloom is shaping up to be among the largest on record, according to county officials. Environmental scientist Sava Verazo cautions that the seaweed can harbor harmful bacteria, so anyone handling it should wear gloves to avoid potential skin contact with pathogens.

SRIA Director Mike Burns underscores the importance of keeping Pensacola Beach clean to maintain its standing as one of the nation's top beach destinations. The grant funding will help support cleanup efforts that protect both the beach's reputation and public health as seasonal blooms continue to affect the area.

item.title: Second Vibrio vulnificus case confirmed in Santa Rosa County
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Santa Rosa County has confirmed a second case of Vibrio vulnificus infection this year, according to the Florida Department of Health. The potentially deadly bacteria has sickened 20 people across Florida in 2024, resulting in four deaths. Vibrio vulnificus occurs naturally in warm coastal and brackish waters and typically enters the body through…
item.content:encoded:
Santa Rosa County has confirmed a second case of Vibrio vulnificus infection this year, according to the Florida Department of Health. The potentially deadly bacteria has sickened 20 people across Florida in 2024, resulting in four deaths.

Vibrio vulnificus occurs naturally in warm coastal and brackish waters and typically enters the body through open wounds or by consuming raw shellfish, particularly oysters. The bacteria can cause severe illness and is especially dangerous for people with weakened immune systems, chronic liver disease, or diabetes.

Health officials are urging residents to take precautions when in coastal waters. Keep open cuts, scrapes, and wounds out of brackish and salt water. If you consume raw oysters or other shellfish, ensure they are thoroughly cooked. Symptoms of infection include fever, chills, weakness, nausea, vomiting, and blistering lesions on the skin. If you experience these symptoms after potential exposure to coastal water or raw shellfish, seek immediate medical attention and inform your healthcare provider of the possible exposure.

item.content:encoded:
Two men are in custody following an armed home invasion robbery at a Destin apartment Friday, with investigators still searching for a third person connected to the incident.

Jared McCree, 27, and Isaiah Webb, 24, are both being held in the Okaloosa County Jail in connection with the robbery. Authorities say the two men forced their way into the apartment and committed the armed robbery.

Deputies are seeking Taylor Nicole Robinson, 28, of Milton, who was present at the apartment during the robbery but left the scene. The Okaloosa County Sheriff's Office says investigators want to confirm Robinson's safety and determine her role in the incident.

Anyone with information about Robinson's whereabouts or the robbery is urged to contact the Okaloosa County Sheriff's Office or Crime Stoppers at 1-800-TIPS. Tips can also be submitted anonymously through the Crime Stoppers website.

The cause of the fire remains under investigation by fire authorities. No additional details about the incident have been released at this time.

item.title: Escambia County Parents Demand DCF Reforms After 'Catastrophic Failure' Report
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Parents rallied Friday in Escambia County demanding accountability from the Department of Children and Families after a grand jury in Florida's Fifth Judicial Circuit released a damning report citing "catastrophic failure" in the agency's duty to protect children and vulnerable adults. The report documented multiple cases where DCF failed to…
item.content:encoded:
Parents rallied Friday in Escambia County demanding accountability from the Department of Children and Families after a grand jury in Florida's Fifth Judicial Circuit released a damning report citing "catastrophic failure" in the agency's duty to protect children and vulnerable adults.

The report documented multiple cases where DCF failed to intervene properly, including situations that resulted in a child's death. The findings have sparked action at the state level, with State Senator Don Gaetz now drafting reform legislation based on the report's thirty-four recommendations. The proposed changes include tighter oversight of DCF contractors and expanded avenues for parents to challenge agency decisions.

Local cases are fueling the push for reform. Gaetz points to the Kenlee Zuraff case in Santa Rosa County as a stark example of DCF overreach. The seven-year-old was removed from her home without sufficient cause, according to Gaetz, and her family has spent nearly two years fighting for reunification. State Senator Jason Pizzo, who represents the Zuraff family in the ongoing case, says the concerns raised by the Fifth Circuit grand jury reflect a troubling pattern affecting families across Florida.

Gaetz's proposed legislation targets two key areas: creating consequences for false information presented to courts during DCF proceedings and establishing stronger oversight mechanisms for DCF's network of contractors statewide. The reform effort reflects growing bipartisan concern that the agency's current structure and accountability measures are insufficient to protect families from wrongful intervention.

item.title: Escambia County Ambulance Strikes Bicyclist During Emergency Response
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: An investigation is underway after an Escambia County ambulance struck a bicyclist Wednesday afternoon while responding to a separate crash in the area. The collision occurred around 1:20 p.m. at W Street and Bayliss Court. The ambulance was operating with lights and sirens engaged at the time of the impact. According to witnesses, the cyclist…
item.content:encoded:
An investigation is underway after an Escambia County ambulance struck a bicyclist Wednesday afternoon while responding to a separate crash in the area.

The collision occurred around 1:20 p.m. at W Street and Bayliss Court. The ambulance was operating with lights and sirens engaged at the time of the impact. According to witnesses, the cyclist rode around a stopped vehicle and entered the ambulance's path, resulting in the crash.

The EMS crew immediately stopped to provide medical treatment to the injured cyclist. A second ambulance was dispatched to respond to the original call that the first unit was answering. The cyclist was transported to the hospital for treatment, though his condition has not been released.

Florida Highway Patrol is conducting the official accident investigation. Escambia County officials say they will also conduct an internal review of the incident as part of standard protocol following accidents involving county emergency vehicles.

item.content:encoded: A Molino resident was sentenced to a year of community control and probation after pleading no contest to felony battery for punching a man outside a Pensacola bar and breaking his jaw. Travis Keith Hethington, 28, reached the plea agreement with prosecutors following the January altercation. The sentencing comes after the incident left the victim with significant facial injuries requiring treatment. Hethington's sentence emphasizes supervised release rather than incarceration, meaning he'll remain in the community under strict conditions while serving out his punishment.

item.content:encoded: An adult male was injured in a shooting early Sunday morning in Atmore, according to the Atmore Police Department. The incident occurred on Carver Avenue near King and Sims streets amid a large gathering of more than 500 people. Officers responded to reports of multiple gunshots fired in the area. In addition to the shooting, police also received reports of a person struck by a vehicle at the scene. The Atmore Police Department is continuing its investigation into the incident.
